candidates.title: Cached developer sessions send cookies outside their recorded origin scope
candidates.description: A developer who previously authenticated to app A can select a different development base B while reusing the default username cache. Before attempting a new login, the helper sends B all cached cookie values, including app-A or separate-IdP cookies whose recorded host/path would exclude B. The lower-trust recipient is B, which has no authority over those source sessions. This is a cookie-disclosure candidate, not a claim of production account takeover; non-public, usable cookies must exist for sensitive impact.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Cache validation reconstructs Cookie from only Netscape name/value columns and ignores recorded domain, host-only, path, secure, and expiry constraints. The default cache identity includes username but no destination. Fresh CookieJar filtering and local mode 0600 do not constrain the manual outgoing header.

trace.description: Operator selects another supported base through --base or DEV_LOGIN_BASE_URL; line 58 preserves the same username cache.
An existing cache is tested against the newly selected base before login unless --force is supplied.
All non-comment records with seven columns are accepted and line 318 discards destination metadata.
fetch sends the aggregate cookie header to the selected base /api/auth/me before examining the response.

evidence.description: Default jar .auth/<user>.cookies is shared across base URLs.
Fresh requests check host and path, showing the intended destination boundary absent from cache validation.
Serialized cookie records include domain, subdomain policy, path, secure, and expiry fields.
Cache validation retains only cookie names and values.
File mode 0600 protects new local files but cannot prevent remote disclosure by the helper.

No real cached credential or deployment was inspected. Sensitive impact requires a usable cookie belonging to a different host/path principal than the selected destination; public fixture passwords alone do not establish it.

validation_plan.local: In the required isolated sandbox, create a dummy Netscape jar containing host-only app-a.test and idp.test cookies. Invoke isJarStillValid with an injected recording fetch and base https://app-b.test. Record only dummy markers; compare the emitted header against CookieJar.header for the same destination. Confirm disclosure occurs even when the mocked response is unauthenticated, then stop.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner can inspect helper configuration and cookie metadata, without exposing values, to establish whether non-public app/IdP sessions are cached and whether developers reuse a username cache across separately administered base URLs.

candidates.title: Untrusted tracker comments can block scheduled container vulnerability scans
candidates.description: A user allowed to comment on an existing automation-owned release tracker issue can place reserved marker text in an ordinary comment. The next scheduled preflight parses that text as automation state and fails; release selection and downstream scans are gated on preflight success. The user need not modify the issue body, labels, repository code, or workflow. Impact is fail-stop monitoring until the comment is removed, not a successful clean scan or release-code compromise.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Issue ownership labels authenticate the issue but not its commenters. Every comment body enters strict automation/continuation marker parsers without checking the producer. A malformed reserved namespace aborts the global terminal-identity preflight, which is required before any release scan.

trace.description: The adapter returns every comment on a tracker issue, including ordinary user comments.
For each labelled owned issue, comments are fetched and passed into state and automation parsers.
Comment bodies are parsed without checking author identity; reserved namespace text is treated as automation metadata.
One namespace with no valid candidate, such as container-vulnerability-reconciliation:, throws.
A terminal-boundary exception produces CLI exit status 1.
Workflow release selection requires tracker-preflight.outcome success, so the failure prevents downstream scan selection.

evidence.description: Ownership-label gating applies to the issue, not the comment producer.
All comments enter the exact marker parser with optional matching; malformed reserved text still throws.
Terminal-identity boundary preflights all owned issues before constructing any boundary.
Scheduled monitor runs the terminal-boundary command before selecting releases.
Source tests explicitly expect malformed automation-marker comments to throw before mutations; these tests were not run.
Generated issue instructions direct human discussion to comments, establishing a mixed-producer surface.

blockers: Required target-execution sandbox is unavailable: bubblewrap namespace creation failed with No permissions to create new namespace. No target code, tests, network, or provider calls were executed.

Repository deployment facts are unavailable: an owned tracker issue must exist, a lower-trust account must be permitted to comment on it, and the scheduled workflow must be enabled. No GitHub API or live repository state was accessed.

validation_plan.local: In the required isolated sandbox, use one valid dummy owned issue and injected tracker adapter. Compare terminal-boundary with an ordinary human comment versus the same fixture plus a non-bot comment containing container-vulnerability-reconciliation:. Verify the latter returns failure without mutation and inspect the workflow gate that excludes selection. Do not contact GitHub or execute a hosted workflow.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner can inspect existing tracker labels, issue lock/comment permissions, and workflow enablement to confirm whether ordinary commenters can supply this input. Do not post a test comment or trigger production monitoring.

candidates.title: Private advisory updates trust a body marker instead of automation ownership
candidates.description: The monitor selects an existing security advisory using only a predictable description marker, then updates draft/triage matches with its dedicated token and confidential scanner details. If a lower-trust private reporter can submit such an advisory, have it returned by this listing, and retain read access after the update, their report can become the recipient of automation-only scan data. The privileged update target is source-visible; hosted reporter submission, mutation permissions, and visibility remain explicit validation prerequisites.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: syncPrivateAdvisories treats inclusion of a deterministic finding fingerprint in a writable description as sufficient authority to select the advisory resource. Neither creator identity nor trusted automation ownership is verified before the privileged PATCH. The fixed repository and draft/triage checks constrain scope but do not establish record ownership.

trace.description: Existing advisory objects, including their descriptions and IDs, enter through the repository security-advisories response.
The first description containing the computed marker is selected with no producer or collaborator check.
The update payload contains confidential finding identifier, package, severity, exceptions, release digests, and installed/fixed versions.
The dedicated private-advisory credential PATCHes the selected draft/triage advisory ID.

evidence.description: Fingerprint is an unkeyed SHA-256 of vulnerability identifier, image, and package; knowing those inputs permits reproducing the marker.
Private advisory payload includes scanner findings and affected release details.
Private reporting must be enabled before the path proceeds; this is checked at runtime.
Description inclusion is the only record selector before the state check and PATCH.
Operator documentation treats scanner observations lacking a public advisory as confidential.

GitHub/provider policy was not inspected: a reporter-created triage/draft advisory must be returned by this endpoint to the bot; the bot token must be permitted to PATCH it; and the reporter must retain read access to the overwritten description. If any prerequisite is false, the claimed disclosure is refuted.
The reporter must know or predict the identifier/image/package tuple for an active confidential scan record. No active record or real finding was inspected.

validation_plan.local: In the required isolated sandbox, inject dummy command responses containing enabled private reporting and a reporter-authored draft or triage advisory with a marker computed from one dummy confidential record. Invoke the synchronization interface with a dummy token and recording command adapter. Verify whether a PATCH selects that reporter-owned advisory and includes the dummy scan details; compare with a nonmatching marker. Do not execute gh or access GitHub.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner must inspect authoritative provider policy and existing non-sensitive metadata to determine private-reporter creation rights, listing inclusion, retained read access, and bot PATCH rights for triage/draft reports. Establish whether the marker inputs are knowable for the intended scanner data. No new report, live mutation, or exposure of confidential content is requested.
